$comment: Invariant ids the P2 round-3 task `p2r3/gapfill-lesson1` contributes to. The list is EMPTY and that is the correct state: INV-PACK-06 is owned by docs/owned/p2-g3-g4.json, INV-PACK-08 by p2-g7.json and INV-PACK-10 by p2-g5-g6.json, and `phase-roster.test.ts` fails on an id claimed twice. This lane adds tests that NAME all three — the coverage map reads test names, not this file — and the claim recorded below is deliberately narrow: an authoring lane plus a length-axis constant can make those three provable and can make them fail; G5/G6 and V1-V6 are what prove them.

contributesTo.INV-PACK-06: V1/V2 from the authoring side, over the nine slots the phase had no content for. `test_INV_PACK_06_exactly_one_candidate_per_lesson_one_slot_is_inside_its_window` lemmatises every row of this lane's shard with the pinned `es_core_news_md`, applies founder ruling B9(a)'s prenominal table, and asserts that each of `u1/l1/s0..s8` has EXACTLY ONE candidate whose lemma set is inside `known | new`, that it carries the lemma G4 reserved for that slot, and that it introduces at most `MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_ITEM` of them. `test_INV_PACK_06_the_lesson_one_ship_texts_are_one_to_twelve_tokens` asserts the same nine sit inside the slot's own token window and that at least one is under `MIN_TOKENS` — i.e. that B9(b) bought something.
contributesTo.INV-PACK-08: V6 register, over EVERY committed shard rather than this lane's. `test_INV_PACK_08_no_authored_candidate_anywhere_is_ustedeo` calls `validators.exercise.register_of` — V6's own function, imported, because it case-folds and strips accents on both sides where a local tokeniser would not — and asserts no row of any of the five shards carries an `usted` marker while the course declares `tu` (`DEFAULT_REGISTER_BY_SLOT['binary_t_v']`). 9,687 rows scanned, 0 offenders. `test_INV_PACK_08_the_ustedeo_scan_would_catch_one` is the falsifier: the scan is a glob and a set intersection and both pass loudly on nothing.
contributesTo.INV-PACK-10: The verbless floor is the cheapest place in the pipeline to introduce a repair path — pad `Hola.` out to three tokens and the gate goes green. `test_INV_PACK_10_the_verbless_floor_is_a_window_and_never_a_patch` runs G5 with the STRICT floor in force over a one-token candidate and asserts the emitted texts are still a subset of the authored texts and that the rejected row is WRITTEN rather than dropped. The source-scanning half of the invariant (no repair-shaped identifier, no string mutator in G5/G6) is unchanged by this lane and still passes: `min_tokens_for_slot` is a comparison, and the only thing it returns is an integer.

heldWithoutAnInvariantId: FOUNDER RULING B9(b). `config/g5.py` gains `MIN_TOKENS_VERBLESS_LESSON = 1`, `VERBAL_POS = {VERB, AUX}` and `min_tokens_for_slot(known_lemmas, new_lemmas, pos_by_lemma, *, base_min_tokens=MIN_TOKENS)`. The relaxation is DERIVED from the slot's own `known | new` against G2's consolidated UD tag per lemma, never declared: `test_the_verbless_floor_is_derived_from_the_ledger_and_cannot_be_declared` pins the signature and fails on any `MIN_TOKENS`-shaped dict in any config module, because B9's option 3 as written is one keystroke from a per-lesson table a curriculum author can set — and a course that could declare `min_tokens: 1` for a lesson that teaches `ser` would ship one-word items for a lesson that can hold a sentence.

The relaxation has to be PROVED and an absent proof keeps the strict floor. One lemma with no tag in the G2 lexicon, or an empty window, returns `MIN_TOKENS`. The empty case is the sharp one: an empty `known | new` is the B1a defect (every gap row G4 emitted carried `known_lemmas: []`), and rewarding it with the loosest possible length axis would have turned that silent bug into 918 one-word 'lessons' every downstream gate would have accepted.

G0's ingest window is untouched. `config/g0.py MIN_TOKENS/MAX_TOKENS` stays [3, 12], a corpus sentence is still filtered at three tokens, and G5's upper bound never moves. Only G5's per-slot lower bound does.

`coursekit gaps <lang>` prints the window the stage will enforce, per slot: `token_window` is `[min_tokens_for_slot(...), MAX_TOKENS]` with `verbless_window: true/false` beside it and a `verbless_slots` count on the header line. It imports G5's predicate rather than re-deriving it (`test_the_brief_uses_g5s_own_predicate_rather_than_a_second_copy`), because a brief telling an author 1 while the stage enforced 3 is how twenty candidates get written and then rejected on length.

B16 option 2, write side: ALREADY LANDED at 61bc272, before this lane branched. `gapfill()` writes `analysis` on every row and `_axis` returns `(axis, analysis)` so that only the two `stale_ledger` short-circuits above the adapter call carry null; `test_an_emitted_candidate_carries_the_analysis_g7_will_read` re-derives it from a second independent adapter call. This lane verified it rather than rewriting it, and adds nothing: the outstanding half of B16 is the READER in `g7_expand.py`, which is the expand lane's file.

The G2 lookup is `stages.g5_gapfill.pos_by_lemma`, and it is deliberately NOT a new upstream requirement. G5 does not `require_successful('g2')`: a missing `banded_lemma` artefact returns `{}`, every caller reads an unknown tag as 'could be a verb', and the length axis is the one G5 has always had. The runlog records `lexicon_pos_rows` so 'no verb in the window' and 'no lexicon to ask' do not read the same afterwards.

measured.$comment: FILLED FROM A REAL LOCAL BUILD — see `build` below. Every number here came out of `uv run coursekit build es` in this worktree with a live LanguageTool 6.6 sidecar, not from a CI summary and not from a replica of the axes.
measured.ledger_digest: 606cd3f645af7b27 on every row — all nine slots of u1/l1 share one window, because `known | new` is the same five lemmas whichever of them the slot is reserved to teach

ship_texts.u1/l1/s1: Buenos días. / Good morning. (new: bueno, 2 tokens)
ship_texts.u1/l1/s2: Hola, buenos días. / Hello, good morning. (new: día, 3 tokens)
ship_texts.u1/l1/s3: Buenas tardes. / Good afternoon. (new: tarde, 2 tokens)
ship_texts.u1/l1/s4: Hola, buenas noches. / Hello, good night. (new: noche, 3 tokens)
ship_texts.u1/l1/s6: Hola, buenas tardes. / Hello, good afternoon.

measured.the_other_nineteen: The same nineteen real level-1 Spanish greetings are offered to every slot, and every one of them reaches outside the five-lemma window: `Buenos días, señora.`, `Buenas tardes, señor.`, `Hola, ¿cómo estás?`, `Hola, ¿qué tal?`, `Adiós, buenas noches.`, `Gracias, buenas tardes.`, `Buenas noches, hasta luego.`, `Hola, me llamo Ana.`, `Muy buenos días.`, `Buenos días a todos.`, `Hola, buenos días y buenas tardes.`, `Buenos días, buenas tardes.`, `Hola, buenas noches, mamá.`, `Buen día, amigo.`, `Hola, mucho gusto.`, `Buenas tardes, encantado.`, `Hola, hasta luego.`, `Buenas noches.`, `¡Buenas tardes!`. They are over-generation, not padding: this is what a generator asked nine times for a greeting in this window produces, and the `out_of_vocabulary` count they generate is the measurement that says the window is five lemmas wide. None is edited to fit (INV-PACK-10), and none of the eleven word lists is among them.
measured.backtranslation_scores: every row 3 or 4, all >= BACKTRANSLATION_MIN_SCORE. A candidate this lane would not ship is not one of the twenty; the nineteen are rejected on VOCABULARY, and scoring them low would be a second reason invented for a rejection that already has one.
measured.word_lists_removed: 55 rows keyed u1/l1 were deleted from content/es/candidates/u01-u06.jsonl — the eleven strings (`Hola, hola.`, `Día, tarde, noche.`, `Bueno, hola.`, `Hola, bueno.`, `Hola, tarde.`, `Hola, noche.`, `Bueno, bueno.`, `Bueno, hola, hola.`, `Día, noche.`, `Tarde, noche.`, `Hola, día, tarde, noche.`) that round 2 documented and refused to ship. They had to go: G5 fills a slot with the first survivor in sorted filename order and `u01-u06.jsonl` sorts before this lane's shard, so leaving them would have made `Hola, hola.` the first item of the Spanish course the moment B9(a) and B9(b) made them admissible.

rekeying.$comment: Ruling B9: re-key only the rows whose ledger_digest actually changes.
rekeying.why: B9(b) moves G5's LENGTH axis and nothing else. It reads no curriculum, changes no `known_lemmas`/`new_lemmas`, and therefore changes no `ledger_digest` and no gap SET: G4's output is byte-identical across the change. The 9,687 rows authored in earlier rounds are untouched and 0 of them go `stale_ledger`. What moves in the regenerated brief is `token_window` on the verbless slots (and the two new fields), and the header `digest` — which is computed over the per-slot `ledger_digest`s only — does not move at all.

blockers: B9(a) IS NOT LANDED, and eight of this lane's nine ship texts are out of vocabulary until it is. The adapter lemma-normalisation table (`buen`/`buena`/`buenos`/`buenas` -> `bueno`) is founder ruling B9(a) and lives in `coursekit/adapters/`, which is `p2r3/lemma-reachability`'s file lane, not this one's. `test_the_pinned_lemmatiser_still_has_not_absorbed_the_prenominal_table` pins the broken state by name and FAILS the day that lane lands, which is the same mechanism `test_the_invocation_build_es_uses_today_leaves_v8_with_nothing` uses for B8; its failure message says to delete `PRENOMINAL_BUENO` and itself, not that the adapter regressed.

THE TABLE AS SCOPED IN B9(a) IS NOT ENOUGH, and this is new. Measured on the pinned `es_core_news_md` 3.8.0: sentence-initial `Buenas noches.` -> `['buenas', 'noches']` and `¡Buenas tardes!` -> `['buenas', 'tardes']`. The PLURAL NOUN is tagged `PROPN` there and is not lemmatised to `noche`/`tarde` at all, so those two canonical greetings stay out of vocabulary even with the prenominal table, and the only surface that reaches the lemma `noche` inside this window is the mid-sentence one (`Hola, buenas noches.` -> `['hola', 'buena', 'noche']`). That is why `s4` ships the three-token form and why `Buenas noches.` is in the reject pool rather than the ship list. The lemma-reachability lane should either extend the table to the PROPN plurals or accept that the course teaches `Buenas noches.` only in the `Hola, ...` frame. B9's write-up does not mention this half.

G5 AND G7 DISAGREE ABOUT WHICH CANDIDATE FILLED A SLOT. G5 marks a slot filled by the FIRST accepted candidate (`if not slot_filled`); `g7_expand.py` builds its lookup with `candidates[key] = row` over every accepted row, so G7 expands the LAST one. Any slot with two or more accepted candidates therefore reports one sentence and ships another, silently. This lane's shard has exactly one accepted candidate per slot so the two agree for `u1/l1`, but that is a property of the content, not of the code, and the 9,687 rows authored in earlier rounds do not have it. Fix belongs in the expand lane (g7_expand.py); recorded here because this lane measured it.

217 rows in `content/es/candidates/u01-u06.jsonl` still carry one of the eleven word lists, for slots of unit 1 OTHER than l1, where they are over-generation the `duplicate` and `out_of_vocabulary` axes deal with. Whether any of them is the FIRST accepted candidate for one of those slots — i.e. whether `Hola, hola.` ships anywhere — is a question about another lane's shard against a real G4 and is not answered here. `test_the_lesson_one_shard_ships_none_of_the_eleven_word_lists` asserts 0 inside u1/l1 and pins the 217 so the number cannot grow unnoticed.

G5's `MIN_TOKENS`/`MAX_TOKENS` are the SPANISH window and are wrong for Japanese. `coursekit.ledger.length_window` reads `config/g1.LENGTH_WINDOW_BY_LANGUAGE`, which is `(3, 12)` for the Latin-script languages and `(4, 18)` for `ja`, because a Mode-A morpheme is a smaller unit than a lemma. `test_the_length_window_cannot_drift_from_the_per_pack_window` pins the es agreement and names the ja mismatch. Rerouting G5's length axis through `ledger.length_window` changes the window of every G5 test and belongs in the round that lands the Japanese pack (P7), not in the round that unblocks lesson 1.

method.authoring: 28 distinct Spanish texts written by hand, each measured with the pinned `es_core_news_md` adapter BEFORE it entered the pool — which is what produced the two traps above and what decided every one of the nine ship texts. Drafts that failed the window were discarded and replaced, never patched (INV-PACK-10): `Buenas noches.` was the intended s4 text and became a reject row when the measurement showed `noches` does not reach `noche`.
method.assignment: Each slot's ship text is the one that carries the lemma G4 reserved for that slot, read off a regenerated `coursekit gaps es` and joined against `build/es/g4/selected.jsonl` rather than against the committed brief's description of itself. s0..s4 reserve `hola`, `bueno`, `día`, `tarde`, `noche` in that order (G4 deals unit 1's target lexemes in authored order and reserves the head of what is still pending); s5..s8 reserve nothing.
method.the_twenty: One admissible candidate plus nineteen over-generated ones per slot, all twenty distinct. A slot padded with the same string twenty times satisfies `MIN_CANDIDATES_PER_SLOT` and defeats it, so `test_the_lesson_one_shard_covers_nine_slots_at_twenty_each` asserts distinctness as well as the count.
method.ledger_fields: `slot`, `ledger_digest` and `new_lemmas` are generated from the brief row, never typed; `test_the_lesson_one_shard_carries_the_ledger_digest_g4_emits_for_that_window` recomputes the digest with `ledger_digest` rather than comparing the committed string to itself.
